exposure: Women without a recorded cancer diagnosis
cohort: 4,978 women diagnosed with breast cancer at ages 15-39 during 2000-2013 in North Carolina
finding: Less than 10% of adolescent and young adult (AYA) breast cancer survivors had a live birth within 10 years of diagnosis, with lower rates observed among those treated with chemotherapy and a higher risk of preterm delivery among those with ER-negative disease.
mod_finding: This study found that births to adolescent and young adult women treated for breast cancer, particularly those with ER-negative disease, were more likely to be preterm.
